title: Helm umbrella chart versioning and TF module interop notes
content:
Context and goals:

This doc collects notes on one practical path for making Helm umbrella charts (multi-chart bundles we ship to customers) comfortably interoperate with our Terraform modules for private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments, while keeping CI/CD, signing, and runtime verification sane. Focus is on upgrade stability, reproducible artifacts, and clear rollback signals.

Why we need this:
- Customers get an umbrella/chart-of-charts that ties together redis, ingress, operator, runtime and observability pieces. Upgrades of the umbrella should never surprise a customer by implicitly changing a TF-managed network or IAM resource.
- Terraform modules own infra (VPCs, subnets, node pools, KMS bindings) and must be the single source of truth for immutable infra ids.
- CI must produce signed, versioned Helm bundles and TF module releases with matching provenance artifacts (SBOM, cosign signature, git SHA) so ArgoCD and on‑cluster agents can validate before applying.

High-level pattern (draft):
1) Infra-first: Terraform applies are run by the customer or by our Private onboarding runner and produce a small outputs JSON containing resource IDs and a Git tag used for the cluster manifest repo.
2) Chart packaging pipeline: A CI job packages the umbrella (helm dependency build -> helm package) and produces a signed bundle (cosign) + sbom. The package contains `values.customer-terraform-output` references that are filled by a manifest generator step using the TF outputs JSON.
3) Manifest repo commit: The generated manifests (kustomize/helmfile or plain helmRelease YAML) are committed into the customer's gitops repo (or a repo we manage for them) with metadata: chart-version, tf-release-id, sbom-sha, cosign-sig, CI-build-url, git-commit.
4) ArgoCD/GitOps: ArgoCD syncs, but a pre-sync hook verifies cosign signature and SBOM fingerprint using a cluster side policy (small admission webhook or ArgoCD Lua hook).
5) Runtime verification: After sync, a smoke-test job (pod) runs basic healthchecks and emits metrics. If smoke-tests fail beyond threshold, automated rollback is triggered by annotating the ArgoCD Application to rollback to previous commit.

Practical CI steps (GitHub Actions example):
- job: build-helm 
  - checkout charts repo
  - helm dependency update umbrella-chart/
  - helm package umbrella-chart/ -d ./artifacts
  - run syft to produce SBOM (spdx/json) for artifacts directory
  - cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY ./artifacts/umbrella-chart-*.tgz
  - upload artifacts and sbom to artifacts bucket (artifact name includes chart version and tf_release_id)
  - generate manifest overlay by calling `tf-output-to-values` script (see snippets below) and commit to gitops repo with message: "release umbrella vX.Y (tf: yyyy-mm-dd:tf-1234)"

TF -> Helm values bridge (tf-output-to-values):
- Input: terraform outputs JSON 
- Output: a YAML fragment with explicit fields used by charts: vpc.id, subnet.ids, k8s.cluster_name, kms.key_alias, registry.endpoint
- Safety: do not inject credentials. Only opaque IDs and DNS names. If we need credentials, use a sealed/secrets provider (e.g. SOPS) and seal them with customer key during onboarding.

Versioning rules (proposal):
- Helm chart versions follow semver. Any change that touches k8s resource shapes increments minor/major as appropriate.
- TF modules use independent versions and have a `module_release_tag` (git tag) included in the manifest commit message.
- The manifest commit must include both a `chart_version` and a `tf_module_tag` string so audits can link the two.
- When chart depends on a TF-managed feature (e.g., enabling nodepool autoscaler via a CRD that requires cloud IAM), require an explicit `tf_compatibility` annotation in Chart.yaml that lists the minimum TF module tag. CI checks this and blocks the manifest commit if mismatch.

Upgrade plan and guardrails:
- Canary window: default 15–30 minutes for small clusters; 60–120 minutes for large clusters.
- Rollout policy: ArgoCD sync waves: infra-adjacent CRDs first -> core runtime -> add-ons. Use `sync-wave` annotations to control order.
- Health checks: readiness probes + job-based smoke-tests (connect to /health, produce sample token, run a light inference if possible). Failures cause alert and canary pause.
- Auto rollback: Annotate Application with `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: RollbackOnFailure=true` or run an automation that reverts to previous commit if N consecutive smoke-tests fail.

Image/artifact provenance (avoid term duplication of other docs but keep behavior):
- All images referenced by charts must be pinned (digest). CI must resolve `image: repo/name:tag` -> `repo/name@sha256:...` and replace values in the packaged chart.
- Signed manifests: we sign the packaged chart tarball and the generated manifest commit. ArgoCD pre-sync hook verifies tarball signature and image digests.
- SBOM: frontend to supply SBOMs for the image layers and packaged charts. Keep SBOM per release and store in artifacts bucket.

Example preflight checklist (what the runner should do before committing manifests):
- [ ] Verify terraform outputs exist and pass shape schema validation
- [ ] Confirm chart version bump or explicit changelog entry
- [ ] Run `helm lint` and `helm template` with customer values
- [ ] Resolve image tags to digests and verify with registry allowlist
- [ ] Generate SBOM and sign artifacts
- [ ] Run smoke-tests against a staging cluster that mirrors production sizing (if available)
- [ ] Commit manifests with metadata and open release ticket (Linear ID in commit)

Runtime verification hooks (ArgoCD integration notes):
- Use argocd pre-sync hook (job) to run `cosign verify` against the chart artifact URL. If verify fails, exit non-zero.
- Implement an ArgoCD Lua policy (or OPA gate outside argocd) that checks manifest annotations for `tf_module_tag` and `chart_version`, and denies sync if mismatch with known-good combos (this requires a small metadata service that returns compatibility matrix).
- Post-sync: run a k8s Job to run smoke-tests. Record status in a release log ConfigMap/CR so SRE can inspect.

Key open questions / TODOs:
- How strictly do we want to force TF-runner-first? Some customers expect us to provision node pools as part of the Helm install flow. Decision pending PD-342.
- KMS/HSM integration for cosign keys in customer-managed deployments. We need an operator-friendly pattern (prefer sealed secrets into cluster and use cosign KMS support?).
- SBOM storage policy: keep SBOMs indefinitely for enterprise customers? default retention 1 year? Need billing impact analysis.
- Who manages the small metadata service for tf<->chart compat check: us (Redwood) or customer? If us, must be multi-tenant and private-per-customer.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Resolve image digests: `skopeo inspect --raw docker://registry/repo:tag | jq -r '.config.digest'` (CI wrapper available in infra repo)
- Simple tf-output-to-values script prototype: `python scripts/tf_output_to_values.py --tf-json out.json --template templates/customer-values.yaml > generated-values/customer.yaml`
- Cosign: `cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY artifacts/umbrella-chart-1.2.3.tgz` and verification in-cluster `cosign verify --key <pubkey> https://artifacts.example.com/umbrella-chart-1.2.3.tgz`

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but still a draft. Looking for feedback on:
  - Whether the tf_compatibility annotation is onerous for customers
  - Feasibility of running staging smoke-tests for every manifest change (cost vs safety)
  - Recommendations for key management patterns in airgapped or customer-KMS setups
